notes.decision: Translated as 'an obeisance with which they pay obeisance to one another' — preserving the cognate construction (verb + cognate object) which the Coptic foregrounds. ⲟⲩⲱϣⲧ here is both the act and the salutation-gesture.

Read as ⲧⲁ-ⲛⲓⲙ ⲧⲉ 'whose is it?' — the disciples' question concerns whom the chirotonia belongs to / pertains to. Could also be 'of what kind' but the genitive interrogative is the more natural reading.

Read as a presentational 'behold' (≈ ⲉⲓⲥ) introducing the enumeration. Form is unusual; possibly a Lycopolitan presentational particle. Translated 'Behold these five kinds:' to fit the catalogue structure that follows.
ⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ here = Sahidic ⲙⲓⲛⲉ 'kind, sort, manner' — distinct from ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness' (different lexeme). Translated 'kinds' consistently throughout.
Read as Lycopolitan variant of ⲡⲥⲏⲩ 'the time' (parallel to ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲁⲡ in lines 2, 21, 30). The orthography ⲥⲭⲩ for ⲥⲏⲩ is unusual but contextually demanded.

Translated tentatively as 'their hand' — possibly a Coptic adaptation of Greek χείρ (cf. χειροτονία in lines 1-4 of this very passage about laying-on of hands). The series 'peace / hand / blessing / joy' fits a sequence of greeting-gestures. Confidence low; could alternatively be a verb of obeisance.
Translated tentatively as 'their joy/triumph' — ⲃⲣⲟ possibly Lycopolitan reflex of a root for exultation/triumph. Fits the sequence of greeting-elements but lexical identification uncertain.
Doubled ⲧ likely scribal dittography or dialectal feature; treated as 'The first' parallel to lines 12, 19, 29.
Translated 'they were sending him forth' — ⲧϩⲡⲟ likely related to ⲑⲡⲟ 'cause to depart, escort.' The ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' confirms a verb of dispatching/sending out.

Lexical identification uncertain. Context ('coming forth to the X of the lower side') suggests a synonym for ⲁⲅⲱⲛ 'contest' or related word for combat/descent. Translated as '[combat]' tentatively in the apparatus.
